title: Build the line from two points, a table, or slope plus a point
subtitle: Linear functions · 41 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **41 of the official questions in Linear functions are this one** — 11 Easy, 22 Medium, 8 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Medium tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- You're given two coordinate points, a table of x and f(x) values, or a slope and one point.
- The answer choices are equations in slope-intercept form, or you're asked for one coefficient, the intercept, a missing table entry, or a combination such as a sum or product of the constants.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Find the slope from any two rows or points: change in output over change in input.
- 2) Get the intercept from the row where x is 0, or by substituting one point into y = mx + b.
- 3) Answer exactly what's asked: the whole equation, one constant, a combination, or a new output.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Enter the points or table as a table, then fit a regression y1 ~ m x1 + b to read off m and b exactly.
You can also graph each answer choice and see which one passes through every point.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You compute the slope as change in x over change in y, or with the subtraction order mismatched.
The trap is also that you give m or b when the question asked for a combination of them, or you pick a choice that only fits one row of the table.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
